pairs.subject: schema-driven-ui
pairs.evidence: src/stores/abilitySpecStore.ts:27 The only file in this context is a 51-line Zustand cache of per-entity GAS ability specs (effects/tagRules/attributes/loadout data that feed editors and C++ codegen, per src/lib/ability/spec.ts:75). It is not a layout spec rendered from a component registry, and a case-insensitive grep of src/stores for renderSpec/nodeKind/componentRegistry/SpecRenderer/uiSpec/layoutSpec found no hits. The map matched this subject only on the tokens 'spec'/'specs'/'design', so the subject's precondition (data describing a UI that a registry-backed renderer realizes) does not hold here.

techniques.evidence: src/stores/abilitySpecStore.ts:8 The slot holds gameplay ability data, not a closed set of UI node kinds.
src/stores/abilitySpecStore.ts:12 This is a map from entity key to data, not from node kind to component. Nothing is rendered by dispatch.
src/stores/abilitySpecStore.ts:17 The store sets edited ability data optimistically. There is no render-time validation door because no UI spec is rendered.
src/stores/abilitySpecStore.ts:49 This is an ordinary store selector hook. There is no spec renderer whose capabilities would need injecting.

pairs.registryProposal: The map's token matcher pairs schema-driven-ui with any context whose code says 'spec'. Here it matched a domain-data 'spec' (a GAS ability spec). Matching could require a co-occurring renderer or registry term (render, kind, component registry) before proposing this subject.
